units.zh: 列傳第六十八 列女 ○阿鄰妻 李寶信妻 韓慶民妻 雷婦師氏 康住住 李文妻 李英妻 相琪妻 阿魯真 撒合輦妻 許古妻 馮妙真 蒲察氏 烏古論氏 素蘭妻 忙哥妻 尹氏 白氏 聶孝女 仲德妻 寶符李氏 張鳳奴
units.en: Biographies 68 — Exemplary Women: The Wife of A Lin; The Wife of Li Baoxin; The Wife of Han Qingmin; Lei Fu, née Shi; Kang Zhuzhu; The Wife of Li Wen; The Wife of Li Ying; The Wife of Xiang Qi; A Luzhen; The Wife of Sahe Nian; The Wife of Xu Gu; Feng Miaozhen; Lady Pucha; Lady Wugulun; The Wife of Su Lan; The Wife of Mang Ge; Lady Yin; Lady Bai; Nie Xiaonü; The Wife of Zhong De; Lady Li of Baofu; Zhang Fengnu
units.literal: Biographies 68 — Exemplary Women: Wife of A Lin; Wife of Li Baoxin; Wife of Han Qingmin; Lei Fu, née Shi; Kang Zhuzhu; Wife of Li Wen; Wife of Li Ying; Wife of Xiang Qi; A Luzhen; Wife of Sahe Nian; Wife of Xu Gu; Feng Miaozhen; Lady Pucha; Lady Wugulun; Wife of Su Lan; Wife of Mang Ge; Lady Yin; Lady Bai; Nie Xiaonü; Wife of Zhong De; Lady Li of Baofu; Zhang Fengnu

units.zh: 漢成帝時，劉向始述三代賢妃淑女，及淫泆奢僭、興亡盛衰之所由，匯分類別，號《列女傳》，因以諷諫。
units.en: Under Emperor Cheng of Han, Liu Xiang first compiled accounts of worthy consorts and virtuous ladies from the Three Dynasties, together with the causes of licentious excess, extravagance, and usurpation—and of dynastic rise and fall—arranged by category in the Biographies of Exemplary Women as a work of moral admonition.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Cheng of Han, Liu Xiang first set forth the worthy consorts and virtuous ladies of the Three Dynasties, and the causes of licentiousness, extravagance, overstepping, rise and fall, flourishing and decline; he gathered and classified them, titled the work Biographies of Exemplary Women, and thereby offered admonition.

units.zh: 范曄始載之漢史。
units.en: Fan Ye was the first to include such accounts in the History of Han.
units.literal: Fan Ye first included them in the History of Han.

units.zh: 古者女子生十年有女師，漸長，有麻枲絲繭之事，有祭祀助奠之事；
units.en: In antiquity a girl of ten was given a female tutor; as she grew she was taught hemp and ramie work, silk and cocoon-reeling, and how to assist at sacrifices and offerings;
units.literal: In antiquity, when a girl reached ten years of age she had a female instructor; as she grew, there were tasks of hemp, ramie, silk, and cocoon-reeling, and tasks of assisting at sacrifices and libations;

units.zh: 既嫁，職在中饋而已，故以無非無儀為賢。
units.en: and once married her sphere was the household alone, so that freedom from fault and impropriety was held the mark of a virtuous wife.
units.literal: once married, her duty was only within the inner kitchen, and therefore to be without fault and without impropriety was deemed worthy.

units.zh: 若乃嫠居寡處，患難顛沛，是皆婦人之不幸也。
units.en: Widowhood, solitude, hardship, and sudden ruin are misfortunes that befall any woman.
units.literal: As for dwelling as a widow in solitude, meeting hardship and destitution—these are all a woman's misfortunes.

units.zh: 一遇不幸，卓然能自樹立，有烈丈夫之風，是以君子異之。
units.en: Yet when misfortune strikes and a woman can still stand firm with the mettle of a resolute man, gentlemen mark her as extraordinary.
units.literal: Yet when one meets misfortune and can stand forth on her own with the spirit of a stern great man, for this reason the gentleman marks her as extraordinary.

units.zh: 阿鄰妻
units.en: The Wife of A Lin
units.literal: Wife of A Lin

units.zh: 阿鄰妻沙裏質者，金源郡王銀術可之妹。
units.en: The wife of A Lin, Shali Zhi, was a younger sister of Yanshuke, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery.
units.literal: The wife of A Lin, Shali Zhi, was the younger sister of Prince of Jinyuan Commandery Yanshuke.

units.zh: 天輔六年，黃龍府叛卒攻鈔旁近部族。
units.en: In the sixth year of Tianfu (1118), mutineers from Huanglong Prefecture raided the neighboring tribes.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, mutinous soldiers of Huanglong Prefecture attacked the nearby tribes of Chao.

units.zh: 是時，阿鄰從軍，沙裏質糾集附近居民得男女五百人，樹營柵為保守計。
units.en: A Lin was away on campaign; Shali Zhi rallied five hundred local men and women, threw up palisades, and prepared to hold out.
units.literal: At that time A Lin was with the army; Shali Zhi gathered nearby inhabitants, obtaining five hundred men and women, and erected palisades as a plan for defense.

units.zh: 賊千余來攻，沙裏質以氈為甲，以裳為旗，男夫授甲，婦女鼓噪，沙裏質仗劍督戰，凡三日賊去。
units.en: When more than a thousand raiders attacked, she improvised armor from felt and banners from skirts, armed the men, set the women to shouting, and herself took sword in hand to direct the fight; after three days the enemy withdrew.
units.literal: More than a thousand bandits came to attack; Shali Zhi used felt for armor and skirts for banners; men were given armor, women raised a clamor; Shali Zhi bore a sword and supervised the battle; in all three days the bandits departed.

units.zh: 皇統二年，論功封金源郡夫人。
units.en: In the second year of Huangtong (1142) she was enfeoffed as Lady of Jinyuan Commandery in recognition of her service.
units.literal: In the second year of Huangtong, for merit she was enfeoffed as Lady of Jinyuan Commandery.

units.zh: 大定間，以其孫藥師為謀克。
units.en: During the Dading era (1161–1189) her grandson Yaoshi was appointed a mouke.
units.literal: During the Dading era, her grandson Yaoshi was made a mouke.

units.zh: 李寶信妻
units.en: The Wife of Li Baoxin
units.literal: Wife of Li Baoxin

units.zh: 李寶信妻王氏。
units.en: The wife of Li Baoxin was a woman of the Wang clan.
units.literal: The wife of Li Baoxin was a woman of the Wang clan.

units.zh: 寶信為義豐縣令，張覺以平州叛，王氏陷賊中。
units.en: Baoxin was magistrate of Yifeng County. When Zhang Jue rebelled at Ping Prefecture, Lady Wang was captured by the rebels.
units.literal: Baoxin was magistrate of Yifeng County; Zhang Jue rebelled with Ping Prefecture, and Lady Wang fell into the hands of the rebels.

units.zh: 賊欲逼室之，王氏罵賊，賊怒遂支解之。
units.en: The rebels tried to take her by force; she cursed them, and in their fury they dismembered her.
units.literal: The rebels wished to force her into the chamber; Lady Wang cursed the rebels, and in anger they dismembered her.

units.zh: 大定十二年，贈「貞烈縣君」。
units.en: In the twelfth year of Dading (1172) she was posthumously granted the title "Chaste and Steadfast County Lady."
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Dading, she was posthumously granted "Chaste and Steadfast County Lady."

units.zh: 韓慶民妻
units.en: The Wife of Han Qingmin
units.literal: Wife of Han Qingmin

units.zh: 韓慶民妻者，不知何許人，亦不知其姓氏。
units.en: The wife of Han Qingmin was a woman of unknown origin and unknown surname.
units.literal: The wife of Han Qingmin—her native place is unknown, and her surname is also unknown.

units.zh: 慶民事遼為宜州節度使。
units.en: Qingmin had served the Liao as military commissioner of Yi Prefecture.
units.literal: Qingmin served the Liao as military commissioner of Yi Prefecture.

units.zh: 天會中，攻破宜州，慶民不屈而死，以其妻配將士，其妻誓死不從，遂自殺。
units.en: During the Tianhui era (1115–1135), when Yi Prefecture fell, Qingmin refused to submit and was put to death; his wife was assigned to the troops, but she swore she would die rather than obey and took her own life.
units.literal: In the Tianhui era, when Yi Prefecture was taken by assault, Qingmin died unyielding; his wife was allotted to officers and soldiers; she vowed to die rather than submit and thereupon killed herself.

units.zh: 世宗讀《太宗實錄》，見慶民夫婦事，歎曰：「如此節操，可謂難矣。」
units.en: When Emperor Shizong read the Veritable Records of Taizong and came upon their story, he sighed and said, "Constancy such as this is truly rare."
units.literal: Emperor Shizong read the Veritable Records of Taizong, saw the affair of Qingmin and his wife, and sighed, saying, "Such constancy may truly be called rare."

units.zh: 雷婦師氏
units.en: Lei Fu, née Shi
units.literal: Lei Fu, née Shi

units.zh: 雷婦師氏，夫亡，孝養舅姑。
units.en: Lei Fu, née Shi, lost her husband and devoted herself to caring for her parents-in-law.
units.literal: Lei Fu, née Shi—her husband died; she filially supported her parents-in-law.

units.zh: 姑病，刲臂肉飼之，姑即愈。
units.en: When her mother-in-law fell ill, she cut flesh from her own arm to feed her, and the elder woman recovered.
units.literal: Her mother-in-law fell ill; she cut flesh from her arm to feed her, and her mother-in-law at once recovered.

units.zh: 舅姑既歿。
units.en: After her parents-in-law had both died,
units.literal: When her parents-in-law had both died.

units.zh: 兄師逵與夫侄規其財產，乃偽立謀證致之官，欲必嫁之。
units.en: her elder brother Shi Kui and her husband's nephew schemed for her property, forged evidence of conspiracy, and hauled her before the magistrate to force her into another marriage.
units.literal: her elder brother Shi Kui and her husband's nephew plotted her property; they falsely set up evidence of conspiracy and brought her before the magistrate, wishing to force her remarriage.

units.zh: 縣官不能辨曲直，師氏畏逼，乃投縣署井中死。
units.en: The magistrate could not tell right from wrong; cornered and afraid, Lady Shi threw herself into the county well and died.
units.literal: The county magistrate could not distinguish right from wrong; Lady Shi, fearing coercion, threw herself into the well at the county office and died.

units.zh: 詔有司祭其墓，賜諡曰「節」。
units.en: The court ordered sacrifices at her tomb and granted her the posthumous name "Chaste."
units.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to sacrifice at her tomb and granted the posthumous name "Chaste."

units.zh: 康住住
units.en: Kang Zhuzhu
units.literal: Kang Zhuzhu

units.zh: 康住住，鄜州人。
units.en: Kang Zhuzhu was from Fu Prefecture.
units.literal: Kang Zhuzhu was a native of Fu Prefecture.

units.zh: 夫早亡，服闋，父取之歸家，許嚴沂為妻。
units.en: Her husband died young; when her mourning ended her father took her home and betrothed her to Yan Yi.
units.literal: Her husband died early; when mourning was completed, her father took her back home and betrothed her to Yan Yi.

units.zh: 康氏誓死弗聽，欲還夫家不可得，乃投崖而死。
units.en: Lady Kang swore she would die rather than consent; unable to return to her husband's household, she leapt from a cliff to her death.
units.literal: Lady Kang vowed to die rather than obey; wishing to return to her husband's house she could not, and thereupon threw herself from a cliff and died.

units.zh: 詔有司致祭其墓。
units.en: The court ordered official sacrifices at her tomb.
units.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to perform sacrifice at her tomb.

units.zh: 李文妻
units.en: The Wife of Li Wen
units.literal: Wife of Li Wen

units.zh: 李文妻史氏，同州白水人。
units.en: The wife of Li Wen, née Shi, was from Baishui in Tong Prefecture.
units.literal: The wife of Li Wen, née Shi, was a native of Baishui in Tong Prefecture.

units.zh: 夫亡，服闋，誓死弗嫁。
units.en: After her husband's death and the end of mourning, she swore she would die rather than marry again.
units.literal: Her husband died; when mourning was completed, she vowed to die rather than remarry.

units.zh: 父強取之歸，許邑人姚乙為妻。
units.en: Her father forced her home and betrothed her to a local man, Yao Yi.
units.literal: Her father forcibly took her back and betrothed her to Yao Yi, a townsman.

units.zh: 史氏不聽，姚訴之官，被逮，遂自縊死。
units.en: Lady Shi refused; Yao brought suit, she was arrested, and she hanged herself.
units.literal: Lady Shi would not obey; Yao appealed to the authorities, she was seized, and thereupon hanged herself.

units.zh: 詔有司致祭其墓。
units.en: The court ordered official sacrifices at her tomb.
units.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to perform sacrifice at her tomb.

units.zh: 李英妻
units.en: The Wife of Li Ying
units.literal: Wife of Li Ying

units.zh: 李英妻張氏。
units.en: The wife of Li Ying was a woman of the Zhang clan.
units.literal: The wife of Li Ying was a woman of the Zhang clan.

units.zh: 英初為監察禦史，在中都，張居濰州。
units.en: Ying first served as investigating censor at the Central Capital while Zhang remained at Wei Prefecture.
units.literal: Ying was at first investigating censor; he was at the Central Capital, while Zhang resided at Wei Prefecture.

units.zh: 貞祐元年冬，大元兵取濰州，入其家，張氏盡以所有財物與之。
units.en: In the winter of the first year of Zhenyou (1213), Mongol forces took Wei Prefecture, entered her home, and Lady Zhang surrendered everything she owned.
units.literal: In the winter of the first year of Zhenyou, the Great Yuan army took Wei Prefecture, entered her house, and Lady Zhang gave them all her possessions.

units.zh: 既而，令張氏上馬，張曰：「我盡以物與汝，猶不見贖邪？」
units.en: Then they ordered her to mount a horse. She said, "I have given you everything I own—is that still not enough to let me go?"
units.literal: Presently they ordered Lady Zhang to mount a horse; Zhang said, "I have given you all my goods—do you still not see fit to ransom me?"

units.zh: 答曰「汝品官妻，當複為夫人。」
units.en: They replied, "You are a ranked official's wife—you will be a lady again."
units.literal: They answered, "You are the wife of a ranked official—you shall again become a great lady."

units.zh: 張曰：「我死則為李氏鬼。」
units.en: Zhang said, "In death I shall be a ghost of the Li household."
units.literal: Zhang said, "If I die I shall be a ghost of the Li clan."

units.zh: 頓坐不起，遂見殺。
units.en: She sat down and would not rise, and they killed her.
units.literal: She sat down abruptly and would not rise, and was thereupon killed.

units.zh: 追封隴西郡夫人，諡「莊潔」。
units.en: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Longxi Commandery with the posthumous name "Solemn and Chaste."
units.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Longxi Commandery, with the posthumous name "Solemn and Chaste."

units.zh: 英仕至御史中丞，有傳。
units.en: Ying rose to censor-in-chief; he has a separate biography.
units.literal: Ying rose in office to censor-in-chief; he has a biography.

units.zh: 相琪妻
units.en: The Wife of Xiang Qi
units.literal: Wife of Xiang Qi

units.zh: 相琪妻欒氏，有姿色。
units.en: The wife of Xiang Qi, née Luan, was a woman of striking beauty.
units.literal: The wife of Xiang Qi, née Luan, had beauty of form.

units.zh: 琪為萊州掖縣司吏。
units.en: Qi was a clerk in Ye County, Laizhou.
units.literal: Qi was a clerk of Ye County in Laizhou.

units.zh: 貞祐三年八月，紅祆賊陷掖縣，琪與欒氏及子俱為所得。
units.en: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyou (1215), Red Hatchet rebels seized Ye County; Qi, Lady Luan, and their son were all taken.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyou, Red Hatchet bandits took Ye County; Qi, Lady Luan, and their son were all captured.

units.zh: 賊見欒悅之，殺琪及其子而誘欒。
units.en: Taken with Luan's looks, the rebels killed Qi and their son and tried to win her over.
units.literal: The bandits, pleased with Luan, killed Qi and his son and tried to entice Luan.

units.zh: 欒奮起以頭觸賊而僕，罵曰：「我豈為犬彘所汙者哉。」
units.en: Luan sprang up, butted a rebel to the ground, and cried, "Would I let dogs and swine defile me!"
units.literal: Luan sprang up, struck the bandit with her head and knocked him down, and cursed, saying, "How could I be defiled by dogs and swine!"

units.zh: 賊怒，殺之。
units.en: Enraged, they killed her.
units.literal: The bandits in anger killed her.

units.zh: 追封西河縣君，諡「莊潔」。
units.en: She was posthumously enfeoffed as County Lady of Xihe with the posthumous name "Solemn and Chaste."
units.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as County Lady of Xihe, with the posthumous name "Solemn and Chaste."

units.zh: 阿魯真，宗室承充之女，胡裏改猛安夾谷胡山之妻。
units.en: A Luzhen was a daughter of the imperial clansman Chengchong and the wife of Jiagu Hushan of the Huligai meng'an.
units.literal: A Luzhen was a daughter of the imperial clansman Chengchong and the wife of Jiagu Hushan of the Huligai meng'an.

units.zh: 夫亡寡居，有眾千餘。
units.en: After her husband died she lived as a widow with more than a thousand followers.
units.literal: Her husband died and she lived as a widow, with more than a thousand followers.

units.zh: 興定元年，承充為上京元帥，上京行省太平執承充應蒲鮮萬奴。
units.en: In the first year of Xingding (1217), Chengchong was grand marshal of the Upper Capital; Taiping of the Upper Capital Branch Secretariat seized Chengchong to answer Pu Xian Wannu.
units.literal: In the first year of Xingding, Chengchong was grand marshal of the Upper Capital; Taiping of the Upper Capital Branch Secretariat seized Chengchong to respond to Pu Xian Wannu.

units.zh: 阿魯真治廢壘，修器械，積芻糧以自守。
units.en: A Luzhen restored ruined fortifications, repaired weapons, and stockpiled fodder and grain to hold out.
units.literal: A Luzhen restored ruined fortifications, repaired weapons, and stockpiled fodder and grain to hold out.

units.zh: 萬奴遣人招之，不從，乃射承充書入城，阿魯真得而碎之，曰：「此詐也。」
units.en: Wannu sent men to summon her, but she refused; he then shot a letter from Chengchong into the city. A Luzhen received it, tore it to pieces, and said, "This is a fraud."
units.literal: Wannu sent men to summon her, but she refused; he then shot a letter from Chengchong into the city; A Luzhen received it and tore it to pieces, saying, "This is a fraud."

units.zh: 萬奴兵急攻之，阿魯真衣男子服，與其子蒲帶督眾力戰，殺數百人，生擒十余人，萬奴兵乃解去。
units.en: When Wannu's troops pressed the attack, A Luzhen dressed in men's clothing and, with her son Pu Dai, directed the defenders in fierce fighting, killing several hundred men and capturing more than ten alive; Wannu's army then withdrew.
units.literal: Wannu's troops pressed the attack; A Luzhen dressed in men's clothing and, with her son Pu Dai, directed the multitude in fierce fighting, killing several hundred men and capturing more than ten alive; Wannu's army then withdrew.

units.zh: 後複遣將擊萬奴兵，獲其將一人。
units.en: Later she again sent generals against Wannu's troops and captured one of his generals.
units.literal: Later she again sent generals against Wannu's troops and captured one of his generals.

units.zh: 詔封郡公夫人，子蒲帶視功遷賞。
units.en: An edict enfeoffed her as Lady of a Commandery, and her son Pu Dai was promoted and rewarded according to merit.
units.literal: An edict enfeoffed her as Lady of a Commandery; her son Pu Dai was promoted and rewarded according to merit.

units.zh: 承充已被執，乘間謂其二子女胡、蒲速乃曰：「吾起身宿衛，致位一品，死無恨矣。
units.en: Chengchong had already been taken prisoner; seizing an opportunity he told his two children, Nühu and Pusunai, "I rose from palace guard service to the first rank; I die without regret.
units.literal: Chengchong had already been taken prisoner; seizing an opportunity he said to his two children, Nühu and Pusunai: "I rose from palace guard service to the first rank; I die without regret.

units.zh: 若輩亦皆通顯，未嘗一日報國家，當思自處，以為後圖。」
units.en: You too have all attained distinction, yet never for a single day have you repaid the state. Consider how you should conduct yourselves and plan for the future."
units.literal: You too have all attained distinction, yet never for a single day have you repaid the state—consider how you should conduct yourselves and plan for the future."

units.zh: 二子乃冒險自拔南走，是年四月至南京。
units.en: The two sons then risked their lives to break free and flee south; in the fourth month of that year they reached the Southern Capital.
units.literal: The two sons then risked their lives to break free and flee south; in the fourth month of that year they reached the Southern Capital.

units.zh: 撒合輦妻
units.en: The Wife of Sahe Nian
units.literal: Wife of Sahe Nian

units.zh: 獨吉氏，平章政事千家奴之女，護衛銀術可妹也。
units.en: Lady Duji was a daughter of Grand Councilor Qianjianu and younger sister of the guardsman Yanshuke.
units.literal: Lady Duji was the daughter of Grand Councilor Qianjianu and the younger sister of the guardsman Yanshuke.

units.zh: 自幼動有禮法，及適內族撒合輦。
units.en: From childhood she was noted for propriety; she married Sahe Nian of the imperial clan.
units.literal: From childhood her conduct observed ritual and law; she was married to Sahe Nian of the inner clan.

units.zh: 閨門肅如。
units.en: Their household was run with strict decorum.
units.literal: The inner gates were solemn and orderly.

units.zh: 撒合輦為中京留守，大兵圍之，撒合輦疽發背不能軍，獨吉氏度城必破，謂撒合輦曰：「公本無功能，徒以宗室故嘗在禁近，以至提點近侍局，同判睦親府，今又為留守外路第一等官，受國家恩最厚。
units.en: Sahe Nian was defender of the Central Capital when the main enemy army laid siege. A carbuncle on his back left him unable to take the field. Lady Duji saw that the city would fall and told him, "You never had great talent; you rose only as a member of the imperial clan—first near the throne as director of the Bureau of Palace Attendants and associate administrator of the Office of Imperial Kin, and now as defender, the highest post on the frontier circuits. The state has favored you beyond measure.
units.literal: Sahe Nian was defender of the Central Capital; the great army besieged it; Sahe Nian had a carbuncle on his back and could not command troops; Lady Duji judged that the city would surely fall, and said to Sahe Nian, "Sir, you originally had no ability; only because of the imperial clan you were once near the forbidden precinct, rising to director of the Bureau of Palace Attendants and associate administrator of the Office of Imperial Kin, and now again you are defender—the foremost office on the outer circuits—and have received the state's favor most thickly.

units.zh: 今大兵臨城，公不幸病，不能戰禦，設若城破，公當率精銳奪門而出，攜一子走京師。
units.en: The enemy is at the walls, and you are too ill to fight. If the city falls, lead your best troops through the gate, take one son, and make for the capital.
units.literal: Now the great army is at the walls; Sir is unfortunately ill and cannot fight in defense; if the city should fall, Sir ought to lead picked troops, break out through the gate, take one son, and flee to the capital.

units.zh: 不能則獨赴京師，又不能，戰而死猶可報國，幸無以我為慮。」
units.en: If you cannot manage that, go to the capital alone; if you cannot do even that, die fighting and you may still repay the state. Do not worry about me."
units.literal: If you cannot, then go alone to the capital; if you cannot do that either, to die fighting may still repay the state—only do not trouble yourself on my account."

units.zh: 撒合輦出巡城，獨吉氏乃取平日衣服妝具玩好布之臥榻，資貨悉散之家人，豔妝盛服過於平日，且戒女使曰：「我死則扶置榻上，以衾覆面，四圍舉火焚之。
units.en: While Sahe Nian went out to inspect the walls, Lady Duji spread her everyday clothes, cosmetics, and treasures on the couch, gave her valuables to the household, dressed more richly than ever, and told her maids, "When I die, lay me on the couch, cover my face with a quilt, and burn me on all sides.
units.literal: Sahe Nian went out to inspect the walls; Lady Duji then took her usual clothes, toilet articles, and cherished objects and spread them on the couch, distributed all valuables to the household, adorned herself more splendidly than on ordinary days, and moreover charged the maids, saying, "When I die, set me on the couch, cover my face with a quilt, and raise fire all around to burn me.

units.zh: 無使兵見吾面。」
units.en: Let no soldier see my face."
units.literal: Do not let the soldiers see my face."

units.zh: 言訖，閉門自經而死。
units.en: With that she shut the door and hanged herself.
units.literal: When she had spoken, she closed the door and hanged herself.

units.zh: 家人如言，臥屍榻上，以衾覆之。
units.en: The household did as she had said, laid her on the couch, and covered her face.
units.literal: The household did as she had said, laid the corpse on the couch, and covered it with a quilt.

units.zh: 撒合輦從外室，家人告以夫人之死，撒合輦拊榻曰：「夫人不辱我，我肯辱朝廷乎！」
units.en: When Sahe Nian returned, they told him she was dead. He struck the couch and cried, "My wife did not shame me—shall I shame the court!"
units.literal: Sahe Nian came from the outer room; the household told him of the lady's death; Sahe Nian struck the couch and said, "My lady did not disgrace me—would I disgrace the court!"

units.zh: 因命焚之。
units.en: He ordered the fire lit.
units.literal: He thereupon ordered her burned.

units.zh: 年三十有六。
units.en: She was thirty-six.
units.literal: Her years were thirty-six.

units.zh: 少頃，城破，撒合輦率死士欲奪門出，不果，投壕水死，有傳。
units.en: Soon the city fell. Sahe Nian led a band of men who tried to fight their way out but failed, then threw himself into the moat and drowned. He has a separate biography.
units.literal: Shortly thereafter the city fell; Sahe Nian led death-defying troops wishing to break out through the gate, but did not succeed, and threw himself into the moat and died; he has a biography.

units.zh: 許古妻
units.en: The Wife of Xu Gu
units.literal: Wife of Xu Gu

units.zh: 許古妻劉氏，定海軍節度使仲洙之女也。
units.en: The wife of Xu Gu, née Liu, was a daughter of Zhongzhu, military commissioner of the Dinghai Army.
units.literal: The wife of Xu Gu, née Liu, was the daughter of military commissioner of Dinghai Army Zhongzhu.

units.zh: 貞祐初，古挈家僑居蒲城，從留劉氏母子于蒲，仕於朝。
units.en: Early in Zhenyou, Gu moved his household to Pucheng, left Lady Liu and their sons there, and took office at court.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, Gu took his family to sojourn at Pucheng, leaving Lady Liu and her sons at Pu while he took office at court.

units.zh: 既而，兵圍蒲，劉謂二女曰：「汝父在朝，而兵勢如此，事不可保。
units.en: When troops besieged Pu, Liu told her two daughters, "Your father is at court, but with the army pressing us like this, nothing is safe.
units.literal: Presently troops besieged Pu; Liu said to her two daughters, "Your father is at court, yet the military situation is thus—affairs cannot be assured.

units.zh: 若城破被驅，一為所汙奈何？
units.en: If the city falls and we are driven away, what if we are violated?
units.literal: If the city falls and we are driven off, what if we are defiled?

units.zh: 不若俱死以自全。」
units.en: Better that we all die and keep our honor intact."
units.literal: Better to die together and preserve ourselves."

units.zh: 已而，攻城益急，於是劉氏與二女相繼自盡。
units.en: The assault grew fiercer, and Lady Liu and her two daughters took their lives one after another.
units.literal: Presently the assault on the city grew fiercer; thereupon Lady Liu and her two daughters in succession killed themselves.

units.zh: 有司以聞於朝，四年五月，追封劉氏為郡君，諡曰「貞潔」，其長女諡曰「定薑」，次「肅薑」，以其事付史館。
units.en: Officials reported the matter to court. In the fifth month of the fourth year, Lady Liu was posthumously enfeoffed as Commandery Lady with the posthumous name "Chaste and Pure"; her elder daughter received the posthumous name "Dingjiang" and the younger "Suojiang"; the Historiography Office was ordered to record the affair.
units.literal: The authorities reported to court; in the fifth month of the fourth year, Lady Liu was posthumously enfeoffed as Commandery Lady, with the posthumous name "Chaste and Pure"; her elder daughter was given the posthumous name "Dingjiang," the younger "Suojiang"; the affair was entrusted to the Historiography Office.

units.zh: 馮妙真
units.en: Feng Miaozhen
units.literal: Feng Miaozhen

units.zh: 馮妙真，刑部尚書延登之女也。
units.en: Feng Miaozhen was a daughter of Yandeng, Minister of Justice.
units.literal: Feng Miaozhen was the daughter of Minister of Justice Yandeng.

units.zh: 生十有八年，適進士張綎。
units.en: At eighteen she married the jinshi Zhang Chao.
units.literal: At eighteen years of age she was married to the jinshi Zhang Chao.

units.zh: 興定五年，綎為洛川主簿。
units.en: In the fifth year of Xingding (1221) Chao was registrar of Luochuan.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Xingding, Chao was registrar of Luochuan.

units.zh: 大元兵破葭州、綏德，遂入鄜延。
units.en: Mongol forces took Jia Prefecture and Suide and advanced into the Yan-Yan region.
units.literal: The Great Yuan army took Jia Prefecture and Suide, and thereupon entered the Yan-Yan region.

units.zh: 鄜人震恐具守備，守臣以西路輸芻粟不時至，檄慥詣平涼督之。
units.en: The people of Fu were terrified and made ready to defend the city. Because fodder and grain for the western route were late, the defending official ordered Chao to Pingliang to hurry the supplies.
units.literal: The people of Fu were alarmed and made full preparations for defense; the defending official, because fodder and grain for the western route did not arrive on time, issued an order that Chao proceed to Pingliang to supervise it.

units.zh: 時延登為平涼行省員外郎，綎欲偕妙真以往，妙真辭曰：「舅姑老矣。
units.en: Yandeng was then associate administrator of the Pingliang Branch Secretariat. Chao wanted Miaozhen to go with him, but she refused: "My parents-in-law are old.
units.literal: At that time Yandeng was associate administrator of the Pingliang Branch Secretariat; Chao wished to take Miaozhen along, and Miaozhen declined, saying, "My parents-in-law are old.

units.zh: 雖有叔姒，妾能安乎。
units.en: Though there is an aunt-in-law, how could I be at ease leaving them?
units.literal: Though there is an aunt by marriage, how could your handmaid be at ease?

units.zh: 子行，妾留奉養。」
units.en: You go, my lord; I will stay to care for them."
units.literal: My lord may go; your handmaid will remain to serve and support them."

units.zh: 十一月，洛川破，妙真從舅姑匿窟室，兵索得之。
units.en: In the eleventh month Luochuan fell. Miaozhen hid with her parents-in-law in a cave, but soldiers found them.
units.literal: In the eleventh month Luochuan fell; Miaozhen followed her parents-in-law into hiding in a cave-room, and the soldiers searched and found them.

units.zh: 妙真泣與舅姑訣曰：「婦生不辰，不得終執箕帚，義不從辱。」
units.en: Weeping, she took leave of them: "I was born under an unlucky star and cannot serve you to the end; I will not submit to shame."
units.literal: Miaozhen wept and took leave of her parents-in-law, saying, "This wife was born untimely and cannot to the end wield broom and dustpan; by right I will not submit to disgrace."

units.zh: 即攜三子赴井死。
units.en: She took her three sons and threw herself into a well.
units.literal: Thereupon taking her three sons she went to a well and died.

units.zh: 縣人從而死者數十人。
units.en: Several dozen people in the county followed her example and died.
units.literal: Several tens of county people followed her in death.

units.zh: 明年春，綎發井得屍，殯於縣之東郭外。
units.en: The following spring Chao opened the well, recovered the bodies, and buried them outside the eastern gate of the county seat.
units.literal: The next spring Chao drew the well and obtained the corpses, and buried them outside the eastern suburb of the county.

units.zh: 死時年二十四。
units.en: She was twenty-four.
units.literal: At death her years were twenty-four.

units.zh: 蒲察氏
units.en: Lady Pucha
units.literal: Lady Pucha

units.zh: 蒲察氏，字明秀，鄜州帥訥申之女，完顏長樂之妻也。
units.en: Lady Pucha, styled Mingxiu, was a daughter of Neshen, military commander of Fu Prefecture, and the wife of Wanyan Changle.
units.literal: Lady Pucha, style name Mingxiu, was the daughter of the commander of Fu Prefecture Neshen and the wife of Wanyan Changle.

units.zh: 哀宗遷歸德，以長樂為總領，將兵扈從。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong moved the court to Guide, Changle was appointed chief commander and led troops in the imperial escort.
units.literal: Emperor Aizong moved to Guide; Changle was made chief commander and led troops in escort.

units.zh: 將行，屬蒲察氏曰：「無他言，夫人慎毋辱此身。」
units.en: Before he left, he told Lady Pucha, "I will say nothing more—only take care not to bring shame upon yourself."
units.literal: As he was about to depart, he charged Lady Pucha, saying, "No other words—Madam, take care not to disgrace this person."

units.zh: 明秀曰：「君第致身事上，無以妾為念。
units.en: Mingxiu replied, "Devote yourself to the sovereign; do not worry about me.
units.literal: Mingxiu said, "My lord need only devote your person to serving the sovereign—do not think of your handmaid.

units.zh: 妾必不辱。」
units.en: I shall not disgrace myself."
units.literal: Your handmaid will surely not disgrace herself."

units.zh: 長樂一子在幼，出妻柴氏所生也，明秀撫育如己出。
units.en: Changle had a young son by his former wife, Lady Chai; Mingxiu raised him as her own.
units.literal: Changle had one son still young, born of his divorced wife the Chai clan; Mingxiu reared him as if born of her own body.

units.zh: 崔立之變，驅從官妻子于省中，人自閱之。
units.en: During Cui Li's mutiny, the wives and children of court officials were herded into the provincial compound so that each man could pick among them.
units.literal: In Cui Li's mutiny, the wives and children of attendant officials were driven into the provincial offices, each man to examine them for himself.

units.zh: 蒲察氏聞，以幼子付婢僕，且與之金幣，親具衣棺祭物，與家人訣曰：「崔立不道，強人妻女，兵在城下，吾何所逃，惟一死不負吾夫耳。
units.en: When she heard, she entrusted her young son to the servants with gold and coins, prepared her own burial garments and offerings, and bade her household farewell: "Cui Li is a villain who seizes men's wives and daughters; with the enemy at the walls I have nowhere to flee. Only by dying can I keep faith with my husband.
units.literal: When Lady Pucha heard, she entrusted the young son to maidservants and also gave them gold and coins, personally prepared clothes, coffin, and sacrificial objects, and took leave of her household, saying, "Cui Li is without the Way, forcibly taking men's wives and daughters; soldiers are below the walls—where could I flee? Only death can fail not to wrong my husband.

units.zh: 汝等惟善養幼子。」
units.en: See only that you raise the boy well."
units.literal: You need only well rear the young son."

units.zh: 遂自縊而死，欣然若不以死為難者。
units.en: She then hanged herself, serene as though death were no hardship at all.
units.literal: Thereupon she hanged herself and died, gladly as if she did not regard death as difficult.

units.zh: 時年二十七。
units.en: She was twenty-seven.
units.literal: At the time her years were twenty-seven.

units.zh: 烏古論氏
units.en: Lady Wugulun
units.literal: Lady Wugulun

units.zh: 烏古論氏，伯祥之妹，臨洮總管陀滿胡土門之妻也。
units.en: Lady Wugulun was a younger sister of Boxiang and the wife of Tuoman Hutumen, superintendent of Lintao.
units.literal: Lady Wugulun was the younger sister of Boxiang and the wife of Tuoman Hutumen, superintendent of Lintao.

units.zh: 伯祥朝貴中聲譽藉甚，胡土門死王事。
units.en: Boxiang enjoyed great renown among the court elite; Hutumen died in the service of the state.
units.literal: Boxiang's reputation among the court nobility was very great; Hutumen died in royal service.

units.zh: 崔立之變，衣冠家婦女多為所汙，烏古論氏謂家人曰：「吾夫不辱朝廷，我敢辱吾兄及吾夫乎。」
units.en: During Cui Li's mutiny many women of respectable families were violated. Lady Wugulun told her household, "My husband did not shame the court—how could I shame my brother and my husband?"
units.literal: In Cui Li's mutiny, many women of gentry families were defiled by him; Lady Wugulun said to her household, "My husband did not disgrace the court—how dare I disgrace my elder brother and my husband!"

units.zh: 即自縊。
units.en: She hanged herself at once.
units.literal: She thereupon hanged herself.

units.zh: 一婢從死。
units.en: One maid died with her.
units.literal: One maid followed her in death.

units.zh: 素蘭妻
units.en: The Wife of Su Lan
units.literal: Wife of Su Lan

units.zh: 參政完顏素蘭妻，亡其姓氏。
units.en: The wife of Grand Councilor Wanyan Su Lan is a woman whose surname is not recorded.
units.literal: The wife of Grand Councilor Wanyan Su Lan—her surname is lost.

units.zh: 當崔立之變，謂所親曰：「吾夫有天下重名，吾豈肯隨眾陷身以辱吾夫乎。
units.en: When Cui Li's mutiny broke out, she told those close to her, "My husband's name stands high throughout the realm—how could I follow the crowd into ruin and shame him?
units.literal: At the time of Cui Li's mutiny, she said to those close to her, "My husband has a weighty name throughout the realm—how could I be willing to follow the crowd into ruin and disgrace my husband!

units.zh: 今日一死固當，但不可無名而死，亦不可離吾家而死。」
units.en: To die today is only right, but I must not die without honor, nor die outside my own home."
units.literal: To die today is indeed fitting, but one must not die without a name, nor die away from my household."

units.zh: 即自縊於室。
units.en: She hanged herself in her chamber.
units.literal: She thereupon hanged herself in her chamber.

units.zh: 忙哥妻
units.en: The Wife of Mang Ge
units.literal: Wife of Mang Ge

units.zh: 溫特罕氏，夫完顏忙哥，五朵山宣差提控回裏不之子也，系出蕭王。
units.en: Lady Wentehan was married to Wanyan Mang Ge, son of the commissioner Huilibu of Wuduo Mountain and a descendant of Prince Xiao.
units.literal: Lady Wentehan—her husband Wanyan Mang Ge was the son of the Xuan Commissioner and Titikong Huilibu of Wuduo Mountain, descended from Prince Xiao.

units.zh: 忙哥叔父益都，節度秦州，為大元兵所攻，適病不能軍，忙哥為提控，獨當一面。
units.en: Mang Ge's uncle Yidu, military commissioner of Qin Prefecture, was attacked by Mongol forces; when illness left him unable to command, Mang Ge as titikong held the line alone.
units.literal: Mang Ge's uncle Yidu was military commissioner of Qin Prefecture; he was attacked by the Great Yuan army, happened to fall ill and could not command troops; Mang Ge as titikong alone held one front.

units.zh: 兵退而益都死，忙哥以城守功世襲謀克，收充奉禦。
units.en: After the enemy withdrew Yidu died; for his defense of the city Mang Ge inherited the rank of mouke and was appointed a palace attendant.
units.literal: When the army withdrew Yidu died; Mang Ge, for merit in defending the city, inherited the mouke rank in perpetuity and was enrolled as palace attendant.

units.zh: 及崔立之變，忙哥義不受辱，與其妻訣。
units.en: When Cui Li's mutiny erupted, Mang Ge refused to submit to shame and bade his wife farewell.
units.literal: When Cui Li's mutiny came, Mang Ge by righteousness would not accept disgrace, and took leave of his wife.

units.zh: 妻曰：「君能為國家死，我不能為君死乎。」
units.en: His wife said, "If you can die for the state, cannot I die for you?"
units.literal: His wife said, "My lord can die for the state—can I not die for my lord?"

units.zh: 一婢曰：「主死，婢將安歸。」
units.en: A maid said, "When my master dies, where shall I go?"
units.literal: A maid said, "When the master dies, whither shall the maid return?"

units.zh: 是日，夫婦以一繩同縊，婢從之。
units.en: That day husband and wife hanged themselves together on one rope, and the maid followed.
units.literal: That day husband and wife hanged themselves together on one rope, and the maid followed them.

units.zh: 尹氏，完顏豬兒之妻也。
units.en: Lady Yin was the wife of Wanyan Zhuer.
units.literal: Lady Yin was the wife of Wanyan Zhuer.

units.zh: 豬兒系出蕭王，天興二年正月從哀宗為南面元帥，戰死黃陵岡。
units.en: Zhuer was of the line of Prince Xiao; in the first month of the second year of Tianxing (1233) he followed Emperor Aizong as southern-route grand marshal and was killed at Huangling Mound.
units.literal: Zhuer was descended from Prince Xiao; in the first month of the second year of Tianxing he followed Emperor Aizong as southern-route grand marshal and died in battle at Huangling Mound.

units.zh: 其妻金源郡夫人聞豬兒死，聚家資焚之，遂自縊，年三十一。
units.en: His wife, Lady of Jinyuan Commandery, on hearing of his death gathered the family wealth, burned it, and hanged herself. She was thirty-one.
units.literal: His wife, Lady of Jinyuan Commandery, on hearing of Zhuer's death gathered the household wealth and burned it, then hanged herself; her years were thirty-one.

units.zh: 豬兒贈官，弟長住即日詔補護衛。
units.en: Zhuer was granted posthumous honors; his younger brother Changzhu was appointed a guardsman the same day.
units.literal: Zhuer was granted posthumous office; his younger brother Changzhu was that same day ordered by edict to fill a guardsman's post.

units.zh: 白氏，蘇嗣之之母，許州人，宋尚書右丞子由五世孫婦也。
units.en: Lady Bai was the mother of Su Sizhi, a native of Xu Prefecture and the fifth-generation daughter-in-law of Ziyou, Right Vice Director of the Song Secretariat of Works.
units.literal: Lady Bai was the mother of Su Sizhi, a native of Xu Prefecture and daughter-in-law in the fifth generation of Ziyou, Right Vice Director of the Song Secretariat of Works.

units.zh: 初，東坡、潁濱、叔党俱葬郟城之小峨嵋山，故五世皆居許昌。
units.en: At first Dongpo, Yinbin, and Shudang were all buried at Little Emei Mountain in Jia County, and for five generations the family lived at Xuchang.
units.literal: At first, Dongpo, Yinbin, and Shudang were all buried at Little Emei Mountain in Jia County, and for five generations the family all resided at Xuchang.

units.zh: 白氏年二十余即寡居，服除，外家迎歸，兄嫂竊議改醮。
units.en: Lady Bai was widowed in her twenties; when mourning ended her maternal family welcomed her back, and her elder brother and sister-in-law secretly discussed remarriage.
units.literal: Lady Bai was widowed in her twenties; when mourning ended her maternal family welcomed her back, and her elder brother and sister-in-law secretly discussed remarriage.

units.zh: 白氏微聞之，牽車徑歸，曰：「我為蘇學士家婦，又有子，乃欲使我失身乎。」
units.en: Lady Bai faintly heard of it, took her carriage and went straight home, saying, "I am a wife of the Su Scholar's household, and I have a son—would you make me lose my chastity?"
units.literal: Lady Bai faintly heard of it, took her carriage and went straight home, saying, "I am a wife of the Su Scholar's household, and I have a son—would you make me lose my chastity?"

units.zh: 自是，外家非有大故不往也。
units.en: From then on she did not visit her maternal family except for great mourning occasions.
units.literal: From this time forth she did not visit her maternal family except for great mourning occasions.

units.zh: 嘗于宅東北為祭室，畫兩先生像，圖黃州、龍川故事壁間，香火嚴潔，躬自灑掃，士大夫求瞻拜者往往過其家奠之。
units.en: She once built a sacrificial chamber northeast of the residence, painted portraits of the two masters, and illustrated Huangzhou and Longchuan stories on the walls; the incense offerings were kept scrupulously clean, and she personally swept and sprinkled; gentlemen seeking to pay reverence often passed her home to offer sacrifice.
units.literal: She once made a sacrificial chamber northeast of the residence, painted portraits of the two masters, and illustrated Huangzhou and Longchuan stories on the walls; the incense offerings were kept scrupulously clean, and she personally swept and sprinkled; gentlemen seeking to pay reverence often passed her home to offer sacrifice.

units.zh: 天興元年正月庚戌，許州被兵，嗣之為汴京廂官，白拜辭兩先生前曰：「兒子往京師，老婦死無恨矣，敢以告。」
units.en: On gengxu, the first month of the first year of Tianxing (1232), Xu Prefecture was overrun by troops. Sizhi was a Bianjing bureau official. Lady Bai took leave before the two masters' portraits, saying, "My son is going to the capital; this old woman dies without regret—I report this to you."
units.literal: On gengxu, the first month of the first year of Tianxing, Xu Prefecture was overrun by troops; Sizhi was a Bianjing bureau official; Lady Bai took leave before the two masters' portraits, saying, "My son is going to the capital; this old woman dies without regret—dare I report this."

units.zh: 即自縊於室側。
units.en: She then hanged herself beside the chamber.
units.literal: She thereupon hanged herself beside the chamber.

units.zh: 家人並屋焚之。
units.en: Her family burned the house together with her.
units.literal: Her family burned the house together with it.

units.zh: 年七十餘。
units.en: She was more than seventy.
units.literal: Her years were more than seventy.

units.zh: 嗣之本名宗之，避諱改焉。
units.en: Sizhi's original name was Zongzhi; it was changed to avoid taboo.
units.literal: Sizhi's original name was Zongzhi; it was changed to avoid taboo.

units.zh: 聶孝女
units.en: Nie Xiaonü
units.literal: Nie Xiaonü

units.zh: 聶孝女，字舜英，尚書左右司員外郎天驥之長女也。
units.en: Nie Xiaonü, styled Shunying, was the eldest daughter of Tianji, associate administrator of the Left and Right Offices of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Nie Xiaonü, style name Shunying, was the eldest daughter of Associate Administrator of the Left and Right Offices of the Secretariat Tianji.

units.zh: 年二十三，適進士張伯豪。
units.en: At twenty-three she married the jinshi Zhang Bohao.
units.literal: At twenty-three years of age she was married to the jinshi Zhang Bohao.

units.zh: 伯豪卒，歸父母家。
units.en: When Bohao died she returned to her parents' home.
units.literal: Bohao died; she returned to her parents' home.

units.zh: 及哀宗遷歸德，天驥留汴。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained in Bian (Kaifeng).
units.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained at Bian.

units.zh: 崔立劫殺宰相，天驥被創甚，日夜悲泣，恨不即死。
units.en: Cui Li seized and murdered the chief councilor; Tianji was gravely wounded, wept day and night, and wished only that he might die.
units.literal: Cui Li seized and killed the chief councilor; Tianji was wounded severely, wept day and night in grief, and hated that he did not die at once.

units.zh: 舜英謁醫救療百方，至刲其股雜他肉以進，而天驥竟死。
units.en: Shunying sought every physician and remedy, even cutting flesh from her thigh and mixing it with other meat for him to eat, but Tianji died all the same.
units.literal: Shunying sought physicians and tried every method of healing, even cutting flesh from her thigh mixed with other meat to present to him, yet Tianji in the end died.

units.zh: 時京城圍久食盡，閭巷間有嫁妻易一飽者，重以崔立之變，剽奪暴淩，無複人理。
units.en: The capital had been besieged so long that food was gone; in the streets men sold their wives for a single meal. With Cui Li's mutiny came plunder and violence until human decency itself seemed lost.
units.literal: At that time the capital had been besieged long and food was exhausted; in the lanes and alleys some sold wives for a single full meal; added to Cui Li's mutiny were plunder, robbery, and violent abuse—human reason no longer remained.

units.zh: 舜英頗讀書知義理，自以年尚少艾，夫既亡，父又死非命，比為兵所汙，何若從吾父于地下乎。
units.en: Shunying was well read and understood moral principle. Still young and fair, with her husband dead and her father killed violently, she thought it better to join her father in the grave than to be violated by soldiers.
units.literal: Shunying had read books and knew righteousness and principle; she considered that her years were still young and fair, her husband already dead, her father also dead by violence—compared with being defiled by soldiers, how much better to follow my father in the underworld!

units.zh: 葬其父之明日，絕脰而死。
units.en: The day after her father's burial she broke her own neck and died.
units.literal: On the day after burying her father she broke her neck and died.

units.zh: 一時士女賢之，有為泣下者。
units.en: Men and women of the day praised her virtue; some wept at her story.
units.literal: Gentlemen and ladies of the time honored her; some wept for her.

units.zh: 其家以舜英合葬張伯豪之墓。
units.en: Her family buried her beside Zhang Bohao.
units.literal: Her family buried Shunying together in Zhang Bohao's tomb.

units.zh: 仲德妻
units.en: The Wife of Zhong De
units.literal: Wife of Zhong De

units.zh: 完顏仲德妻，不知其族氏。
units.en: The wife of Wanyan Zhong De is a woman whose clan and surname are not recorded.
units.literal: The wife of Wanyan Zhong De—her clan and surname are unknown.

units.zh: 崔立之變，妻自毀其容服，攜妾及二子紿以采蔬，自汴走蔡。
units.en: During Cui Li's mutiny she disfigured her face and clothing, took a concubine and her two sons, disguised herself as a vegetable gatherer, and fled from Bian to Cai.
units.literal: In Cui Li's mutiny, the wife herself disfigured her face and dress, took a concubine and two sons, pretended to be gathering vegetables, and fled from Bian to Cai.

units.zh: 蔡被圍，丁男皆乘城拒守，謂仲德曰：「事勢若此，丈夫能為國出力，婦人獨不能耶！」
units.en: When Cai was besieged and every able man manned the walls, she told Zhong De, "Matters stand as they do—if men can serve the state, why cannot women?"
units.literal: When Cai was besieged, all able-bodied men mounted the walls to resist; she said to Zhong De, "Affairs are thus—can a husband exert strength for the state while a woman alone cannot!"

units.zh: 率諸命婦自作一軍，親運矢石於城下，城中婦女爭出繼之。
units.en: She rallied the noble wives into a corps of their own, hauled arrows and stones to the foot of the wall herself, and women throughout the city rushed out to join her.
units.literal: She led the titled ladies to form an army of their own, personally transported arrows and stones below the walls, and women in the city vied to come out and follow her.

units.zh: 城破自盡。
units.en: When the city fell she took her own life.
units.literal: When the city fell she killed herself.

units.zh: 寶符李氏
units.en: Lady Li of Baofu
units.literal: Lady Li of Baofu

units.zh: 哀宗寶符李氏，國亡從後妃北遷，至宣德州，居摩訶院，日夕寢處佛殿中，作幡旆。
units.en: Lady Li of Baofu, an attendant of Emperor Aizong, followed the imperial consorts north after the fall of the state. At Xuande Prefecture she lived in the Mahā Monastery, slept in the Buddha hall by day and night, and made Buddhist banners.
units.literal: Lady Li of Baofu, attendant of Emperor Aizong—when the state perished she followed the empresses and consorts north; arriving at Xuande Prefecture she dwelt at the Mahā Monastery, day and night sleeping in the Buddha hall, making banners and pennants.

units.zh: 會當赴龍庭，將發，即於佛像前自縊死，且自書門紙曰：「寶符禦侍此處身故。」
units.en: When the time came to go to the khan's court and she was about to set out, she hanged herself before the Buddha image and wrote on the door, "Baofu, imperial attendant, died here."
units.literal: When she was to go to the Dragon Court and was about to depart, she hanged herself before the Buddha image, and moreover wrote on the door paper, "Baofu, imperial attendant, died here."

units.zh: 後人至其處，見其遺跡，憐而哀之。
units.en: Those who came afterward saw what she had left and mourned her with pity.
units.literal: Later people coming to the place saw her traces and pitied and mourned her.

units.zh: 張鳳奴
units.en: Zhang Fengnu
units.literal: Zhang Fengnu

units.zh: 天興元年，北兵攻城，矢石之際忽見一女子呼於城下曰：「我倡女張鳳奴也，許州破被俘至此。
units.en: In the first year of Tianxing (1232), as northern troops assaulted the walls amid a hail of arrows and stones, a woman suddenly called out from below: "I am the courtesan Zhang Fengnu; when Xu Prefecture fell I was captured and brought here.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianxing, as northern troops attacked the city amid arrows and stones, suddenly a woman was seen calling below the wall, saying, "I am the courtesan Zhang Fengnu; when Xu Prefecture fell I was captured and brought here.

units.zh: 彼軍不日去矣，諸君努力為國堅守，無為所欺也。」
units.en: Their army will leave before long. Hold the city for your country and do not be deceived."
units.literal: That army will depart within days; gentlemen, strive to hold firm for the state—do not be deceived."

units.zh: 言竟，投濠而死。
units.en: When she had finished speaking, she threw herself into the moat and died.
units.literal: When she had spoken, she threw herself into the moat and died.

units.zh: 朝廷遣使馳祭於西門。
units.en: The court sent an envoy to offer sacrifice at the West Gate.
units.literal: The court dispatched an envoy to offer swift sacrifice at the West Gate.

units.zh: 正大、天興之際，婦人節義可知者特數人耳。
units.en: Between the Zhengda and Tianxing eras, only a handful of women whose constancy is known can be named.
units.literal: In the interval between Zhengda and Tianxing, women whose chastity and righteousness are known amount to only a few persons.

units.zh: 鳳奴之事別史錄之。
units.en: Fengnu's story is recorded in another history.
units.literal: Fengnu's affair is recorded in a separate history.

units.zh: 蓋亦有所激雲。
units.en: Perhaps she too had been stirred by what she had seen.
units.literal: Perhaps there was also something that stirred her, it is said.
